fields.title: Every job in kac.yml sits behind the gate
fields.evidence: The `tool` job's log on the pull request, under the step "Run kac.core unit tests".

sections.What it checks:
* [std-CI.GATE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/f8c34ec1d9a282677cda83f6a58b54b1df5c5a81/examples/dog-fooding/standards/workflows.md#gate-the-gate-runs-on-every-pull-request-into-main) says `kac.yml` "**MUST** name every one of its jobs in the
  `needs:` of its `validate` job".
* `eng:std-GATES.BLOCK` says branch policy "**MUST** block a merge while any required check is
  failing". The test checks the half of that `kac.yml` decides: that `validate` fails when a job it needs fails.
sections.How it works:
`WorkflowGateTests` in `tooling/kac.tests` reads `.github/workflows/kac.yml`. The `tool` job runs it under `dotnet test --project tooling/kac.tests`. It asks three things of the `validate` job.

* **Every job is in `needs:`.** The test compares the keys under `jobs:` against `validate`'s `needs:` plus `validate`
  itself. A job added with no line in `needs:` fails. A `needs:` entry listing a job the file no longer declares fails
  as well.
* **The gate runs after a failure.** `validate`'s `if:` is `always()`. Without it, a failed job skips `validate`, and
  GitHub counts a skipped required check as passing.
* **The gate reads the results.** A step of `validate` reads `needs.*.result`. With `always()` and no such step, the
  gate would pass every pull request.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
The test reads `.github/workflows/kac.yml` and no other workflow. The publishing workflows gate nothing, so a job outside `validate`'s `needs:` is a fault only `kac.yml` can have.

The branch rule sits outside the repository. [ctl-0001](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/f8c34ec1d9a282677cda83f6a58b54b1df5c5a81/examples/dog-fooding/controls/0001-merge-gate.md) covers whether it still names `validate`.
